main_text.l: nus ufuramq; cepisti, & alios avare per
injuriam fruaudasti, oblita mei, inquit
X C.
Nónne patrem unum habemus nos o-
mnes? nónne nos Deus unus creavit? cur
prodit frater fratrem, profanando no-
strum fœdus patrium? Proditor est Iu-
daus, fitq; nefas in Israelitis ac Hieroso-
lymis: siquidem profanat Iudaus fanum
Iovæ quod amavit, peregriniq; Dei puel-
lam maritat. Evertet Iehova virum
qui id fecerit, vigilantem & responden-
tem ex Iacobæis tabernaculis, & fertum
armipotenti Iovæ obmoventem. Adde
quod efficitis, ut obtegatur lachrymis a-
ra Iovæ ploratu ac suspiriis, ita ut non
amplius ferta respiciat, neque placami-
na ex vestra manu admittat. Quaretis,
quamobrem? quoniam Iova tibi & tuæ
juventutis uxori conscius est, in quam
tu perfidiosus es, cùm sit tua socia, & tibi
fœderata conjunx. Quod si unus fecit
qui spiritu abundabat, quorsum allega-
tur unus ille[?], qui divinam progeniem

page.notes: Printed text ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page; the paragraph continues on the next page. "Iu-daus" and "o-mnes" keep the printed line-end hyphens. "ille[?]": the mark after "ille" is a small stroke, possibly an abbreviation, and is not clear. "X C." is printed as a bare numeral and letter in the text block, so it is a paragraph, not a heading. "Ezech.22." stands at the end of the first line of the continuing paragraph, inside the text block, not in a margin.
